correctness.rationale: The square-zero vectors have zero e_2 coordinate and x_1=±x_3; the other lines must contain idempotents in S, and the idempotent equations give exactly the stated z_lambda when lambda differs from 2. For an independent plane check, in the basis (u,w,e_2) the products are u²=w²=0, uw=-2u, e_2u=e_2w=0 and e_2²=(lambda/2-2)u+lambda e_2-(lambda/2)w. A plane not containing u has basis w+b u, e_2+a u. Its closure forces b=a=0 by squaring the first vector and multiplying the two, then requires lambda=4. Planes containing u correspond to lines closed under multiplication in the two-dimensional quotient by Ku, which has just the two directions w and e_2-w/2; their preimages are W and S. The intersections are the stated ones, and Ku is an ideal, so both Frattini formulas follow. S²=S explains non-solvability. The reasoning allows characteristic 3 and all other allowed fields. The frozen finite-field checker was inspected but not executed.
